meaning: A trick where someone acts like a trusted person or group to get your money or information.
clues: Someone tricks you to get your money or personal details.
The person pretends to be your bank, the government, or a family member you trust.
The request may arrive by phone, text, or email.
Urgency and threats are common warning signs.
assumes: An advance-fee loan scam promises a loan if you pay a fee first
An investment scam promises profits if you put money into an opportunity
A fake check or overpayment scam sends a bad check and asks you to send some money back

decoys.meaning: A false promise of a loan that asks you to pay a fee first. No loan ever comes.
A false chance to make money asks you to put money into it.
Someone sends a bad check and asks you to send back part of the money.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: If a caller says they are from your bank, hang up and call the number on your card. Do not use the number they give you.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: We trusted a familiar voice, but we still checked the number in the phone book.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: A real office will let you take time to verify. Pressure is a reason to stop.
